extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers, neuro-oncologists and translational immunotherapy investigators working on CAR T cell therapies for pediatric CNS tumours
extracted.subtask_short: phase I GD2-CAR T trial report
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting of a first-in-human phase I dose-escalation clinical trial of autologous GD2–4-1BB–CD3Ζ CAR T cells for H3K27M-mutated diffuse midline gliomas (DIPG and spinal DMG), including trial design, toxicity management, clinical/radiographic outcomes and correlative biomarker studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary objectives of the phase I trial were assessing feasibility of manufacturing, safety and tolerability, and identifying the maximally tolerated dose or recommended phase II dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the predefined primary endpoints to guide trial success; feasibility requires successful manufacture meeting release criteria, safety/tolerability require systematic toxicity monitoring and reporting, and dose-finding requires observing dose-limiting toxicities to define MTD/RP2D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary and exploratory objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of clinical activity was a secondary objective and identifying biomarkers of response was an exploratory objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical activity should be evaluated by predefined clinical and radiographic measures; exploratory biomarker analyses (cytokines, qPCR, scRNA-seq, cfDNA) are used to correlate immune responses with outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient eligibility and screening considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patients enrolled were children and young adults with pontine and spinal cord DMG characterized by H3K27M mutation; all participants were more than 6 months from completion of standard radiotherapy. Patients with bulky thalamic or cerebellar tumours were excluded; Ommaya reservoir placement in patients with DIPG was required to monitor intracranial pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criteria include molecular confirmation of H3K27M, timing after radiotherapy, tumour location/volume constraints; pre-placement of monitoring devices (Ommaya) and exclusion of high-risk bulky lesions are pre-emptive safety measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAR T cell manufacturing and release criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: GD2-CAR T cells were successfully manufactured and met release criteria for all infused patients (Supplementary Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturing must produce autologous CAR T products that meet predefined release specifications (identity, viability, potency, sterility, transgene detection); feasibility is judged by successful generation and release of product for infusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dose and administration regimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Dose level 1 (DL1): 1 × 10^6 GD2-CAR T cells per kg administered intravenously. Patients who exhibited clinical benefit were eligible for subsequent GD2-CAR T cell infusions administered intracerebroventricularly (i.c.v.) via Ommaya without lymphodepletion; selected higher i.c.v. doses were within ranges used on other brain tumour trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial design must specify dose levels, routes (i.v. vs i.c.v.), lymphodepletion status for each administration, and justification referencing precedent dosing ranges; re-treatment criteria and dose conversions (e.g., equivalent per kg) should be clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity monitoring period
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol instituted a 28-day intensive toxicity monitoring period after infusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensive inpatient monitoring window should be predefined (here 28 days) to capture acute CRS, neurotoxicity/TIAN, and other early adverse events requiring rapid intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and taxonomy of neurotoxicity (CRS, ICANS, TIAN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed toxicities included cytokine release syndrome (CRS), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), and tumour inflammation-associated neurotoxicity (TIAN) — CAR T cell-mediated inflammation at sites of CNS disease. Two categories of TIAN were defined: (1) ICP and intracranial space-constraint events secondary to inflammation-induced oedema or CSF obstruction; (2) primary dysfunction of brain/spinal cord structures affected by inflammation resulting in transient worsening of pre-existing deficits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt standardized grading for CRS and ICANS per established definitions; include TIAN as an organ-site-specific neurotoxicity concept for CNS tumours and categorize management urgency by whether ICP is involved vs primarily functional deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity management algorithm and interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The management algorithm incorporated removal of cerebrospinal fluid via Ommaya, hypertonic saline, anti-cytokine agents (e.g., tocilizumab, siltuximab), anakinra (IL-1R antagonist), corticosteroids, continuous CSF drainage, and use of agents (e.g., dasatinib) to dampen CAR T cell activity; neurocritical care precautions were employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specified interventions should be available and promptly applied for ICP elevation/obstructive hydrocephalus and severe neurotoxicity; Ommaya access for CSF removal and continuous drainage is emphasized; anti-cytokine and corticosteroid timing/indications should be protocolized to balance toxicity control and antitumour activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-emptive neurocritical measures and device strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate TIAN risks, the trial excluded patients with bulky thalamic or cerebellar tumours, required Ommaya reservoir placement in DIPG patients to monitor ICP, and instituted a neurocritical care toxicity management algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial protocols for CNS tumours should include pre-treatment surgical/device planning (e.g., Ommaya) and neurocritical care resource allocation when inflammation-induced mass effect is anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of on-target, off-tumour toxicity
rubrics_metrics.description: On-target, off-tumour toxicity (GD2 expression on normal neural tissues) was monitored; no clinical or radiographic indication of on-target, off-tumour toxicity (e.g., painful neuropathy) was observed in these patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring should include clinical surveillance for expected on-target toxicities informed by antigen expression in normal tissues and compare tumour vs normal tissue antigen density; post-mortem tissue and immunohistochemistry/qPCR can document differential expression and CAR infiltration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical and radiographic response assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical benefit was assessed by neurological examination findings and functional improvements (e.g., facial strength, gait, feeding) and radiographic response by MRI (T2/FLAIR signal changes and percentage tumour volume reduction, e.g., ~17–27% reductions reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clinical endpoints (neurological scales, functional measures) and radiographic metrics (sequences, segmentation, percent volume change) prospectively; document timing of assessments relative to infusion (e.g., 2–4 weeks) and correlate with clinical status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlative biomarker measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlative studies included plasma and CSF cytokine profiling (Luminex multiplex), GD2-CAR transgene qPCR (for CAR DNA kinetics), flow cytometry for CAR surface expression, single-cell RNA sequencing of CSF and manufactured products, and ddPCR detection of cell-free tumour H3K27M mutant DNA in CSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correlative assays should be pre-specified, include timing around peak inflammation and intervention timepoints, use validated assays with controls, and be interpreted in context of clinical and radiographic outcomes (e.g., increased CSF cfDNA during peak inflammation suggests tumour killing).

rubrics_metrics.name: CAR T cell kinetics and compartmental analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: CAR T cell expansion and persistence were monitored by qPCR for GD2-CAR DNA in blood and by flow cytometry in CSF; i.c.v. administration yielded higher proportions of CAR T cells in CSF than i.v. at peak inflammation timepoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kinetic monitoring should include serial quantitative measurements (technical replicates), comparison across compartments (blood vs CSF), and interpretation of route-dependent differences in expansion and tissue penetration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-cell transcriptomic and myeloid/lymphoid composition analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing of 65,598 cells (25,598 CSF cells and 40,000 product cells) was used to identify lymphoid and myeloid populations, myeloid activation/suppressive states, Treg abundance, and differences between responders and non-responders (e.g., interferon/PD1 signalling in product associated with reduced activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-throughput single-cell approaches with clear cell numbers, clustering (UMAP/Harmony), differential signature scoring (e.g., immune-activating vs immune-suppressive), and statistical compositional frameworks (e.g., scCODA) to relate cellular states to clinical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cytokine profiling interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro-inflammatory cytokines implicated in CRS (including IL-6) were higher following i.v. than i.c.v. administration in blood, whereas pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, TNF, IL-2, IL-6) were higher in CSF after i.c.v. administration; immunosuppressive cytokines (TGFβ family) were elevated in CSF of a non-responder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cytokine patterns should be analyzed by compartment and correlated with clinical grade of CRS/TIAN and response; ensure technical duplicates and appropriate assay dynamic ranges (note when values exceed upper limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular assay validation and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: ddPCR for H3K27M detection included serial dilution validation against wild-type background and inclusion of negative (water) and positive (conditioned medium from H3K27M-mutated cell cultures) controls; qPCR and other assays used technical replicates (e.g., n=3 for qPCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molecular assays must be validated with dilution series and appropriate positive/negative controls on each run; report replicate numbers and limits of detection/quantitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and reporting standards per Nature reporting summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting summary required inclusion of exact sample sizes (n), whether measurements were from distinct samples or repeated measures, statistical tests and sidedness, covariates, assumptions and corrections, full reporting of statistical parameters, and data/code availability (single-cell data uploaded to GEO GSE186802).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should follow journal reporting checklists: disclose n, statistical methodology (tests, adjustments), effect sizes/confidence intervals, code availability, and full source data deposition for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow cytometry reporting and gating standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow cytometry plots must state marker and fluorochrome, have visible axis scales, use contour/pseudocolor plots, provide numerical values (cell counts or percentages) with statistics, and include representative gating strategies; acquisition aimed for ≥10^6 cells unless limited by sample source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to explicit flow cytometry reporting standards: label axes, show gating strategy and representative plots in supplements, specify instrument/software, cell acquisition numbers and assay limits of detection (here 1 in 10^4 of acquired PBMCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: MRI acquisition and reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: MRI brain and spine were performed at 3T with T2 sequences shown; report area of acquisition and sequence parameters, and present pre- and post-treatment images with quantified tumour volume changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imaging protocols and parameters must be described; provide standardized timepoints and quantitative volumetrics (percent change) and illustrative axial/sagittal images with arrows/annotations for reported radiographic responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, consent and trial registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stanford University IRB approved the clinical study; photos were published with informed consent; clinical trial registration NCT04196413 and study protocol (with amendments) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical reports must include institutional ethics approval, informed consent for identifiable materials, and registry/PROSPERO/clinicaltrials.gov identifiers and accessible protocol documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural transparency for clinical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporting summary states specifics for clinical data collection windows (June 2020–March 2021), enrollment numbers (four patients at DL1), no randomization, no blinding, replication/technical replicate practices (e.g., triplicates for ddPCR and qPCR), and no data exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent declarations about study conduct in early-phase trials (sample size rationale, lack of randomization/blinding where applicable), replication practices for assays, and any exclusions or amendments to protocol.
